chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the contracted slave who fabricated (lied) upon a Muslim man.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped the penalty of the free man, eighty (lashes), whether he has paid something from his contract or has not paid.' It was said to him: 'So if he commits adultery and he is contracted, and has not paid anything from his contract?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the Right of Allah. Fifty lashes are staved off from him, and he is whipped fifty.'

key_terms.افْتَرَى: Fabricated (specifically qadhf, or false accusation of zina)
key_terms.حَدَّ الْحُرِّ: The penalty of the free man (referring to the standard hadd for free individuals)
key_terms.حَقُّ اللَّهِ: Right of Allah (a category of penalty often involving discretion or reduction)
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: Contracted slave (a slave who has agreed to pay a specific sum for his freedom)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for a contracted slave who commits adultery or fabricates a crime?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the nature of the penalty for qadhf (false accusation) and zina (adulition) for a mukatab, noting that while qadhf incurs the full hadd of 80 lashes irrespective of debt, zina is a 'Right of Allah' where the unpaid portion of the contract reduces the penalty to 50 lashes. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the mukatab's financial obligation to his master does not mitigate divine retribution for adultery in the same way it does for other offenses, reflecting the interplay between contractual status and spiritual liability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the contracted (slave) who fabricated upon a Muslim man.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) of the free, eighty (lashes), whether he has paid anything from his contract or has not paid’. It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if he commits adultery and he is contracted, and has not paid anything from his contract?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a Right of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Fifty lashes would be staved off from him, and he would be whipped fifty’.
